:::{#prp-density-limit-right-derivative}
#### The density limit is the right derivative of the CDF

If $X$ is a continuous random variable with CDF $\cdf$,
then for every $x$:

$$\lim_{\change \downarrow 0} \frac{\Pr(x \le X < x + \change)}{\change}
= \lim_{\change \downarrow 0} \frac{\cdff{x + \change} - \cdff{x}}{\change}$$

whenever either limit exists;
the right-hand side is the right derivative of $\cdf$ at $x$.

:::

::: proof

The first two lines of the proof of @thm-density-limit
use only that $X$ is continuous,
so for every $\change > 0$ the two quotients are equal.
Equal functions of $\change$ have the same limit as $\change \downarrow 0$,
or both have none.

:::
